checks.claim: the store's reconciliation report matches what its own journal implies, so the report is derived and not asserted
checks.counterclaim: if the report names gaps the journal cannot support, or omits gaps the journal implies, every gap claim below rests on an unverified summary

checks.claim: A guard decision that never left the host is still nameable as missing, because an expectation was registered before the action ran
checks.counterclaim: if the store holds a verdict for A-1042, or reconciliation cannot name it, the expectation did not do the work claimed

checks.claim: without a prior expectation the same failure leaves no name at all, so M1 depends on the expectation and not on the store noticing something by itself
checks.counterclaim: if A-1043 appears anywhere in the store, the store is naming what it was never told about and M1 is measuring the wrong thing

checks.claim: a verdict committed locally before a failed ship survives, and lands later carrying the time it was decided rather than the time it arrived
checks.counterclaim: if the stored decision timestamp equals the replay step, or the verdict predates the restart, then the record carries recovery time and the claim fails

checks.claim: the timestamp in the store's record is the one the host wrote down before the ship, recovered from a separate file
checks.counterclaim: if the write-ahead log disagrees with the store, one of them was reconstructed after the fact and the timestamp is not independent evidence

checks.claim: the effect did not proceed while the verdict was undurable centrally, so a lost verdict is a failure and not a divergence
checks.counterclaim: if an effect was committed in B, the withheld-effect rule was not being tested

checks.claim: an issued id plus a preserved commitment names the gap and carries its content, so the missing verdict can be described without the host
checks.counterclaim: if reconciliation names C-3003 without its descriptor digest, the commitment did not survive and this is only a name

checks.claim: issuance alone names the gap with no content, so the record knows an action was named and cannot say what it was
checks.counterclaim: if C-3004's gap carries content, the issuance-only case was not isolated

checks.claim: a locally minted id leaves silence: the store cannot name the action at all, and this is the weakest of the three outcomes rather than a variation of the same result
checks.counterclaim: if C-3005 appears anywhere, the silence is not silence and the strongest claim in this row would be overstated

checks.claim: a complete record verifies against the key it carries, and the descriptor digest recomputes from the action rather than being taken on trust
checks.counterclaim: if the signature does not verify over the stored bytes, or the digest does not recompute, the record is only a file that says so

checks.claim: a preserved record whose binding does not verify is quarantined and never counted as verified, and it stays visible rather than being dropped
checks.counterclaim: if an unsigned record is accepted, or disappears, quarantine is doing no work

checks.claim: every artifact uses one newline convention, so a run on Windows is the same bytes as a run on Linux and not a machine-specific rendering of one
checks.counterclaim: if any artifact carries CRLF, the byte-identical claim is false on that platform and the record says more about the operating system than about the failure

checks.claim: every timestamp in every artifact is a counter step, so two runs agree byte for byte
checks.counterclaim: a wall clock anywhere makes the suite non-deterministic and the comparison moot

checks.claim: two runs of the suite produce identical artifacts, so a result can be reproduced by anyone without trusting the machine it ran on
checks.counterclaim: if any artifact differs between runs, the suite reports the machine as much as the failure
